tasks.title: E12 in full from its design
tasks.brief: You are the only coder on epic E12 (Retrieval and typed tool gateway). Implement it in full from its design docs/tdd/E12.md: every section, and every R, V and D of its acceptance matrix with a test, including end to end tests on the real stack. docs/build/E12/PLAN.md and ticket_tasks in docs/build/E12/tasks.json describe one split of this work with briefs, tests and gates: use them as a guide and checklist; the design and docs/SYSTEM.md win where they differ. Build in this order: domain, application, adapters, api, user interface, and run your tests as you go. If an epic you depend on has no code yet, code against its port protocol and the kernel fakes (docs/SYSTEM.md section 10).

tasks.title: Resolve every E12 round-1 blocker and major in one fix pass
tasks.brief:
You are the single coder for the one E12 round-1 fix pass. Read AGENTS.md, docs/SYSTEM.md and docs/requests/COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md first, then docs/tdd/E12.md, docs/product/tdd/E12.md, docs/build/E12/PLAN.md, this task file, docs/build/E12/review-r1.md, the T1 report/violations/gates and all provider designs/ports needed by your bindings. Review findings below are mandatory; they describe independently observed behavior, not coder claims. Edit only the exact owned_paths. No git. No product/design/SYSTEM/coordinator-decision/shared-validator/provider/UI edits. Do not alter files being built by another person. Required shared or provider changes belong to their owner and must be reported to the coordinator with exact evidence; their absence remains an acceptance blocker. Do not create local replacement providers, ledgers, clocks, queues, text matchers, manifest verifiers or a new API. No missing prerequisite permits a skip, xfail, empty test, weakened assertion, relaxed gate or fabricated fallback.

Fix all nine blockers and both majors below. There are no minors. Add a failing regression first for every reproduced defect, implement the E12-owned change, then rerun the full hub suite. Preserve genuine unavailable states while completing the positive paths. The accepted design corrections are the actual E05 caller-UOW MeasurementCommands.propose binding, omission of unsupported architecture.toml and INI import-contract format. None removes product acceptance. Use provider ports and generated effective models exactly; every name must exist in its defining file.

1. [blocker] E12 is not registered as an executable feature. `hub/src/crew_health/tools/module.py:7` registers settings only. It provides none of ToolGateway, ContextBuilderPort, OutputPolicyPort or EffectApplier, no static handlers, no catalog/tokenizer startup binding and no PolicyValidator loader contribution. Only capabilities.py exists among the planned provider handlers. `hub/tests/tools/test_bounds.py:65` actually requires the registry to contain no providers. The real SQLite case at `hub/tests/tools/test_gateway.py:168` proves that the missing turn/call audit registration aborts a denial, not that a functioning gateway commits its audit. This fails E12-01/02/03, SYSTEM 5.12 and E12 sections 4, 5 and 15. Required change: complete the owned adapters and module factories/bindings against the real published owner ports, register the mandatory checks and obtain the shared audit/reference binding. Bind the pinned catalog, vocabulary, tokenizer, prompt serialization, authorized projections and controller effect boundary. Add a real composition test proving positive authorized calls, committed safe denials and optional-provider unavailability. Implement the remaining question, proposal, read and calculation families required by the design; missing providers remain explicit acceptance dependencies, never fabricated implementations or permanent feature removal. Keep E13 routes, E28 plan handlers and provider storage in their owners.

2. [blocker] Critical acceptance and failure tests are absent or assert only component behavior. `docs/build/E12/PLAN.md:35` names four HTTP/SSE scenario files; none exists. `hub/tests/tools/test_privacy.py:11` tests numeric JSON parsing, with no privacy exit. `hub/tests/tools/test_effects.py:61` claims R45/D06/D30/V78 but its Measurements fake merely appends to a Python list; no request, gap, form link, receipt, event or acquisition state is persisted. `hub/tests/tools/test_policy.py:81` claims V63/V84 by comparing strings, without a help or plan owner. There is no test_time.py or test_performance.py. The matrix below identifies every outstanding R/V/D claim. Required change: implement all four planned scenarios through the actual hub, SQLite, owner operations and documented model boundary, including running-server contract checks and rendered D25/D30 evidence through E21. Cover every E12 section 12 test obligation and each applicable AGENTS section 6 fault: crash before/after commit and ACK, disk full/corruption, same-key/different-target and late retry, cancellation/generation fencing, concurrent facts/grants/kit changes, clock correction/restart/mission boundaries, corrupt activation with last-good pins, partial/disagreeing readings, ground outage, absent/incapacitated crew and all privacy exits. Test removal of the gateway check with independent owner denial. Add missing privacy canaries, PDF instruction attacks, positive unavailable-kit persistence, one-action insight/warning behavior and stopped-model safety backups. Do not satisfy traceability by attaching more markers to the existing doubles.

3. [blocker] The gateway accepts structurally wrong and unsafe handler data without the required semantic validation. `hub/src/crew_health/tools/application/gateway.py:156` checks only generic JSON shape/size and ToolResult metadata. It does not validate a tool-specific result schema, support eligibility or the output policy. Admission at line 116 also has no argument-aware object/field authorization or domain policy stage; ScopeAuthority receives only scope. `hub/src/crew_health/tools/application/policy_service.py:40` checks shared text matches and exact tuple membership, but never invokes the warning predicate, guidance/plan/help guards or typed support verification. `require_warning_authority` has no production caller. Reviewer reproduction using the existing gateway() test factory: set HandlerOk.data to `{"quality":"rejected","quantity":{"value":123,"unit":"1"},"level":"emergency","action":"clear"}` and call get_capabilities. Result is `ok` with all those bytes preserved. This does not itself clear a warning, but it violates the closed typed result and failed-value exclusion requirements before any controller uses it. Required change: validate arguments and each result against the pinned per-tool contract and authorized owner projection, apply support restrictions, and integrate the complete mandatory policy/owner guards before effects or output can leave the stage. Require those bindings for positive acceptance. Preserve storage/auth/config errors. Add regressions for wrong-tool payloads, finite failed numerical canaries, foreign references, nested forbidden text and warning/help/plan actions, plus independent owner-state assertions.

4. [blocker] Deadline and policy limits are not enforced as specified. `hub/src/crew_health/tools/application/gateway.py:139` invokes the handler first, then compares only this call's duration with the original deadline.duration. The deadline anchor is never examined and duration is incorrectly called remaining. Each call gets that full allowance again. Reviewer reproduction: move the existing one-second scope deadline anchor back one day; execute returns `ok` and the handler runs once. A hung handler is also never interrupted by the post-return check. Lines 50 and 51 read only HubSettings; the stricter pinned assistant-policy iteration and timeout limits are never consulted. The current budget test explicitly accepts 32 calls although the package policy example limits iterations to 8. Required change: consume the shared correction-aware deadline/lease authority before dispatch and after completion, intersect actual remaining time, tool/turn settings and pinned policy limits, and enforce external cancellation in the owner adapter outside a writer transaction. Unknown/expired time must prevent execution. Test expired anchors, accumulated calls, forward/backward corrections, process epoch changes, cancellation, hanging providers and a policy limit lower than the hub ceiling. Do not implement another scheduler or clock algorithm.

5. [blocker] Configuration can authorize prohibited retrieval queries. `hub/src/crew_health/tools/application/retrieval_service.py:44` checks only vocabulary count and string length; validate at line 58 treats exact membership as proof of public safety. Reviewer reproduction constructs PublicQueryBoundary with `https://example.invalid`, `../eval/vault` and `SELECT * FROM records`; all three validate unchanged. The current adversarial test at `hub/tests/tools/test_retrieval_service.py:115` only proves those strings are absent from one test vocabulary. It does not prove a configuration edit cannot weaken the safety boundary. This contradicts E12 4.1 and AGENTS rules 1 and 6. Required change: validate the real versioned public vocabulary/field mapping at startup, independently enforce the non-configurable executable-query/path/URL prohibitions, and reject known private identities/record content before E10 or embedding handoff. A bare tuple plus caller-supplied release ID is not verified provenance. If public scope cannot be established, stay unavailable. Add adversarial vocabulary-edit tests and assert the search/embedder is never called, alongside ordinary public literal queries that remain usable.

6. [blocker] Context drops the clinical meaning and lineage needed to interpret its values. `hub/src/crew_health/tools/domain/support.py:14` has no indicator/question/choice identity, answer value/text, conflict relationship, source revision or freshness-policy/correction provenance. `hub/src/crew_health/tools/application/context_builder.py:27` serializes only those reduced fields. An answer can say present without saying which question it answers; a quantity cannot identify its measured indicator. Two unequal readings in `hub/tests/tools/test_context_builder.py:54` are called a conflict but no conflict flag or relationship is asserted or representable. The closed kind set also cannot carry the required capabilities and unresolved gaps. An optional daily-check/routine negative can be discarded because line 167 promotes only answers and observations to required sections. Required change: bind the owner-authored typed projections and preserve the identifiers, configured clinical content, values/presence, original and corrected times with trusted freshness provenance, revisions, conflict links and gap/capability facts required by E12 sections 3/3.1/4.4. Keep private text excluded. Make every configured required fact, explicit negative, red flag and material contradiction non-droppable regardless of kind. Add distinct-question/indicator cases, explicit disagreement assertions, required negative overflow and clock-segment/uncertainty cases. Never guess freshness or reconstruct clinical meaning from opaque IDs.

7. [blocker] Retrieval does not preserve the required contradiction/history information. `hub/src/crew_health/tools/application/retrieval_service.py:249` reads only the first history page and ignores next_cursor. Reviewer reproduction with the actual EvidenceQueryService and 51 memberships: read_approved for evr_50 returns InReleaseHistory and the next owner page contains it, but E12 raises CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE. `_passage` at line 266 drops the owner's use status and successor reference; RetrievedPassage has no discrepancy lineage. Successful search always returns an empty history tuple. The single superseded-passage test at `hub/tests/tools/test_retrieval_service.py:207` never compares contradictory old/new content. Required change: consume bounded owner history pagination and discrepancy/successor data with exact release/use/hash identities, retain both sides visibly as appropriate, and ensure only eligible current content can support a claim. If a bound prevents complete inspection, return an explicit incomplete limitation, not a false missing-pin explanation. Add actual provider tests with a later-page pin, contradictory versions, withdrawal and unapproved neighbors; prove the controller exposes the history without accepting it as current support. R21/V24/D10 remain unaccepted until that integration works.

8. [blocker] The recorded task gates are not runnable acceptance gates. `docs/build/E12/tasks.json:162` selects missing test_time.py; later gates select missing conftest.py, token_counter.py, thirteen handler files, test_performance.py and the absent scenario directory. All six generated `.toml` import configurations fail parsing with `Invalid value (at line 2, column 16)` because the generator emits INI. T1's top-level gates list is empty, so running only tasks[].gates would verify nothing. Required change: restore the real owned implementation/test deliverables rather than deleting selections or creating empty passing files. The coordinator must propagate the evidenced INI suffix correction to the task-gate definitions and maintain a nonempty complete F1 gate list. Preserve the original commands and their failures in this review; corrected commands must still run import-linter. Scenario commands must collect and execute real E12 cases using the hub's pinned environment, without loading the engine conftest, skips or PATH workarounds.

9. [blocker] Shared gates fail and their current assurance inventory does not establish E12 safety. `scripts/validate_hub.py:330` selects E01 tests and line 344 reads only E01's design. In this review the actual INI import-linter gate reports 179 kept and 4 broken contracts, including tools through config, knowledge and measurement ports. The full hub suite has 3 failures and 57 warnings. Corpus validation has 74 errors; coverage validation cannot parse its report within its traversal bound; safety reports complexity 19 and 755 conditions lacking evidence; mutations reports 761 mutants lacking evidence; trace lacks T-E01-10 and T-E01-19. The E21 runner has 44 failures, including every claimed E12 demo. Required change: resolve the E12 consumer/import and evidence issues without weakening rules, and have the owning teams correct the shared tool/provider failures and extend the existing per-file coverage, safety-condition, mutation and trace checks to E12. Re-run all gates with actual E12 evidence and a fresh sequential coverage report. Outside-owner failures remain blockers for greenlight, not permission for the F1 coder to edit shared files. The three hub failures are the two effective intake contract tests and knowledge's real SQLite lexical-index test; none is waived as unrelated.

10. [major] The benchmark and reference measurements are not delivered. `hub/src/crew_health/tools/adapters/cli_bench.py:168` computes metrics from supplied rankings but has no executable retrieval runner, frozen common-population execution, applicability-failure report or measured latency. fixtures/tools/manifest.json and source-checklist.json are absent. test_performance.py is absent. E12 4.2/11/12 and T3/T6 require the real dev comparison and reference evidence before selecting settings. Required change: implement the executable benchmark using E18's permitted dev partition and independently checked labels/source checklist, run lexical/dense/hybrid and the configured optional reranker against one frozen population, retain all failures in denominators, validate references against the pinned corpus, and report applicability errors and measured latency without imputation. Add the marked reference tests for the specified gateway/context/retrieval/RSS/cancellation envelope and record the real environment/pins. An unavailable method must remain explicitly unavailable, never a claimed comparison result.

11. [major] The manifest adapter duplicates an existing owner mechanism. `hub/src/crew_health/tools/adapters/cli_bench.py:91` reimplements FrozenManifest parsing, manifest digest verification, file hashing and path verification. The owner already implements FrozenManifest and FreezeLibrary.verify_tree in `eval/bench/src/crew_health_bench/freeze.py:20` and `eval/bench/src/crew_health_bench/freeze.py:115`; E21 consumes that shared library. Required change: use the E18 verifier through its published boundary for the offline benchmark, retaining only E12-specific dev-only/profile/suffix restrictions and bounded reads in E12. Do not create another manifest format, generic verifier or clinical file port. Test integration with an actual E18-created manifest, hash drift, traversal, symlink and adjacent holdout denial. Resolve any packaging seam with its owner instead of duplicating it.


Required acceptance checklist:

Time correction, mission boundaries, last-good activation, warning preservation and independent stopped-model safety are not established by current E12 tests.


Gate execution: run the focused regression command, all original task gates, all T1.gates commands and the added corrected INI commands. The retained historical .toml commands are known to fail because they select the wrong parser; their coordinator-owned task-definition correction is required before greenlight. Do not change the generator to emit a different format, silently drop those gates, or claim their corrected replacements pass unless actually run. The original commands are retained for exact review reproducibility, and the additional INI commands prove the real import rules. Missing selected files must be implemented with real assertions rather than empty files. Run coverage-producing commands sequentially and validate a freshly generated full-suite report. Have E01 include E12 in the existing per-file coverage/condition/mutation/trace gates; E12 must not build a parallel gate or edit the shared one. Obtain provider-owner fixes for the four transitive import failures, 74 corpus errors, three hub failures and failed assurance inventory. E21 must provide real rendered D25/D30 results; the current 44 awaiting_request failures are not acceptance. No PATH workaround, runtime pin bypass, broad ignore or changed test expectation may hide a failure. Report exact commands, pass/fail/warning counts and unresolved owner dependencies. Deliver real reference measurements with environment and pins, and the coordinator AI-use handoff naming Joaquin Castellano. Never claim clinical validation or whole-epic completion from component coverage. Use English, no em/en dashes or spaced hyphen used as a dash.
